messages:
maria: Heads up — apiserver p99 latency spiking in sa-east1, controller-manager workqueue climbing fast, suspect NAT peer drift between sa-east1 peers. seeing leader hops around 1804242380-1804242420 :eyes:
jonathan: yup, etcd leader flips line up with the apiserver p99 spikes. RTT to peers jumped ~200ms. kube-controller-manager retries piling up (reconcile latency >30s).
ashok: any obvious packet loss on the peering?
maria: short tcpdump shows repeated retransmits toward peer-02. pasted minimal excerpt:
```
14:12:04.123 IP sa-ctrl-01 > sa-ctrl-02: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:12:04.326 IP sa-ctrl-02 > sa-ctrl-01: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960
(retries, dup acks)
```
kai: also seeing provisioning-controller backoff for GPU claims — ~120 pending pods stuck in Pending with Events: "failed attaching volume / waiting for GPU". Backlog likely amplifying controlplane churn.
jonathan: can we short-circuit GPU-heavy jobs to eu-west1 while we stabilize sa-east1? latency to customers won't be ideal but keeps controlplane healthy. what's the cost delta?
ashok: rough calc: shifting 50 vGPUs -> eu-west1 increases hourly infra by ~$0.10/GPU-hour due to spot premium + egress. At 50 GPUs that's ~$5/hr -> ~$120/day. Also some scheduling friction.
maria: proposal: divert 20% of new GPU claims (not existing) to eu-west1 for 1 hour as a canary, monitor apiserver p99, etcd leader stability, and controller-manager queue. If stable, gradually increase.
jonathan: +1. i'll create a route override and add a canary placement rule. I'll annotate the provisioner: `placement.override=eu-west1 (canary)` and target only new claims.
sre-bot: action: route-override/gpu-eu-canary created by jonathan at 1804242530.
kai: applied. watching metrics: apiserver_p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 520ms within 3m. controller manager queue depth halved.
maria: leader flips stopped after diverting traffic. seems like peering jitter was triggering raft election timeouts and cascading retries.
ashok: i'll open INF-8932 to record cost impact + follow-up: file a peering ticket with infra-net to investigate packet loss between sa-east1 peers.
jonathan: after 30m of stable metrics i'll roll back the override and then schedule a controlled roll (or keep if infra requests it). thanks all.
maria: leaving the canary for 30 more mins, will post results. :thumbsup:
